title: Final: the big cleanup
sub: GC, finalizers and resources: test yourself
cards/0/task: Clean up everything: the session with its cart, and the logger with its finalizer.
cards/1/q: An object is in Gen 2. A Gen 0 collection just ran. What happened to it?
cards/1/explain: A Gen 0 collection doesn't look at older generations. And there is no Gen 3.
cards/2/q: What counts as a root? Select all that apply.
cards/2/options/1: A local variable of a running method
cards/2/options/2: A field of a garbage object
cards/2/explain: A generation doesn't make an object a root. Roots are thread stacks and static fields.
cards/3/q: From what size does an object go to the LOH?
cards/4/q: The connection must close even if Count throws an exception
cards/4/explain: using var calls Dispose at the end of the block, however you leave it.
cards/5/q: Why is SafeHandle better than your own finalizer?
cards/5/options/0: Critical finalization and protection against closing a handle mid-call
cards/5/explain: SafeHandle closes the handle reliably and won't let the number be reused while a call is in progress.
cards/6/q: A references B, B references A, and nothing else references them. What happens during a collection?
cards/6/explain: They can't be reached from the roots, so they're garbage. The cycle doesn't save them.
cards/7/q: Where is the memory leak here?
cards/7/explain: Market is static and lives forever. The subscription holds on to every PriceView. You need to unsubscribe, for example in Dispose().
cards/8/q: An object with a finalizer became garbage. What's the minimum number of collections before its memory is freed?
cards/8/explain: The first puts it on the finalization queue, the second frees it.
